oneTimers: A $476M pre-tax paper loss from revaluing equity investments sits in other expense — the main reason GAAP EPS ($0.25) trails non-GAAP EPS ($0.88).
The year-ago comparison is flattering in reverse: Q3 2025 net income of $6.6B included a $4.9B one-time tax benefit and a $1.5B investment gain.
verdict: Trips and orders pushed Gross Bookings up 20% to $59.8B for the fifth straight quarter, and the core business set profit records — but a $476M paper loss on equity investments cut GAAP net income to $512M.
otherDetail: A $616M net other expense — mostly a $476M paper loss from revaluing Uber's equity investments — plus $152M of interest expense and a $42M loss from equity-method investments, partly offset by $176M of interest income.
footerNote: Net income of $569M includes $57M attributable to non-controlling interests; $512M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $0.25 EPS figure). Cost of revenue is shown excluding depreciation and amortization, exactly as Uber reports it.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: non-GAAP EPS $0.88 — the gap is a paper loss

takeaways.title: Bookings growth won't slow down
takeaways.text: Gross Bookings — everything riders and eaters spent on the platform — grew 20% to $59.8B, the fifth straight quarter at 20%+, with record audience and engagement.

takeaways.title: Core profit hit a record
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP operating income rose 38% to $2.3B (3.9% of bookings, a record) and Adjusted EBITDA grew 31% to $3.0B — the underlying business has never been more profitable.

takeaways.title: GAAP profit tells a noisier story
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.25 vs $0.88 non-GAAP, almost entirely because of a $476M paper loss on equity investments. A year ago the same line (plus a $4.9B tax benefit) flattered GAAP profit instead.

follow100Note: Kept-as-profit includes −$4.29 of other expense per $100 of revenue.
